curriculum.lesson_evidence: Respectful communication uses words, tone and body language that show you value the other person. It includes listening without interrupting, using polite words, taking turns, asking questions and disagreeing without put-downs. Tone and body language can change the meaning of words, so a calm voice, eye contact if comfortable and an open posture help. Respect also means accepting different ways of communicating, including signing, writing or a quiet style.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Rewrite 'That's a stupid idea!' so that it disagrees respectfully. Add the tone and body language you would use.

FEEDBACK
Rewrite: 'I'm not sure that will work, could we try this instead?' Tone: calm. Body: face the speaker. A respectful disagreement keeps the idea and removes the insult.

WATCH FOR
Believing words are the only thing that matters. Tone of voice and body language also send messages.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Collect three examples of respectful and three of disrespectful communication from a story, a show or your day (without naming real people). For each, name the words, tone and body language and rewrite the disrespectful ones respectfully.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example: two students disagree about a game. Respectful: 'I see it differently. Can I tell you my idea?' Tone: calm. Body: facing the person. Disrespectful: rolling eyes and saying 'that's a dumb idea'. The same disagreement is handled with respect when words, tone and body language all match.

TRY FIRST
Rewrite 'That's a stupid idea!' so that it disagrees respectfully. Add the tone and body language you would use.

FEEDBACK
Rewrite: 'I'm not sure that will work, could we try this instead?' Tone: calm. Body: face the speaker. A respectful disagreement keeps the idea and removes the insult.
teach_steps.explain:
Respectful communication uses words, tone and body language that show you value the other person. It includes listening without interrupting, using polite words, taking turns, asking questions and disagreeing without put-downs. Tone and body language can change the meaning of words, so a calm voice, eye contact if comfortable and an open posture help. Respect also means accepting different ways of communicating, including signing, writing or a quiet style.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the cues, rules or choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For any movement, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby, move at your own comfortable level and stop if anything hurts or feels unsafe. You may always choose a gentler version or only describe the movement. One deliberate, reasoned change is more useful than a longer answer.
